title: 2022 FIFA World Cup
prose:
The 2022 FIFA World Cup, staged in Qatar from 20 November to 18 December, was the first edition held in the Arab world and the Middle East, and the first contested in November and December rather than the traditional May-July window, a shift made to avoid Qatar's summer heat. It was also the last tournament to feature 32 teams before the expansion to 48 in 2026. The 32 nations were drawn into eight groups of four, playing round-robin matches before a single-elimination knockout phase comprising the round of 16, quarter-finals, semi-finals, a third-place play-off, and the final. The tournament set a record for the most goals scored in the 32-team format, with every participating team scoring at least one goal, and drew a total attendance of 3,404,252 across the competition, an average of 53,191 per match.

The group stage produced one of the great upsets when Saudi Arabia stunned eventual champions Argentina 2-1. Argentina recovered from that opening defeat to march on, while Morocco wrote history of its own, defeating Spain and Portugal to become the first African nation to reach a World Cup semi-final, ultimately finishing fourth. Croatia claimed third place.

The final at Lusail Stadium in Lusail pitted Argentina against France in a contest of remarkable swings. Lionel Messi converted a penalty in the 23rd minute and Angel Di Maria added a second in the 36th, before Kylian Mbappe struck twice in quick succession, a penalty in the 80th minute and another goal in the 81st, to force extra time at 2-2. Messi restored Argentina's lead in the 108th minute, only for Mbappe to complete his hat-trick from the penalty spot in the 118th, making it 3-3. Argentina prevailed 4-2 on penalties. Mbappe became only the second man to score a hat-trick in a World Cup final after Geoff Hurst in 1966, yet finished on the losing side, while also claiming the Golden Boot as top scorer with eight goals. Messi won the Golden Ball, becoming the first player to take the award twice after his 2014 honour, lifting the trophy as the crowning achievement of his career and securing Argentina's third title, after 1978 and 1986.
